title: Artists who evolve; broadening taste to Led Zeppelin, Stevie Wonder and Marvin Gaye
summary: He never lost interest in an artist who evolved, learned to appreciate rock and soul, and plays soul tunes now.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Are there any artists — I’m not sure how to phrase this — that got to a point with their music that you didn’t like it anymore? I’ll use an example. When I was younger I didn’t know who John Coltrane was yet, when I was in junior high, and someone said, “Well you better listen to John Coltrane” and I went and bought “Om.” And my first exposure to John Coltrane was, wow, I could not handle that. Has there been an artist that you admired that kept progressing to the point where he’s lost me.

No. No. I just appreciate the fact that that person or artist is still trying to push the envelope and is still trying to find something different or another facet of their creative nature. So right, Coltrane in ’57 is very different than ’66, but it’s still Coltrane. So I appreciate the ride. I really do. So I don’t know, I get a lot of people who are going well Wayne Shorter sure doesn’t sound like he did in 1961. He’s not supposed to. That’s like me saying well man, some of your high school friends say well you don’t look like you did when you were 17, well you’re not supposed to. You would like to maybe or maybe not. But that’s the way this thing is, it’s different. And so these trees, they look different every year. The dogs, as they age, they look different. That’s what this thing is. We’re trying to evolve. And I think a lot of times we have trouble because we’re not trying to evolve. We’re trying to stay in that place as a listener maybe. But that creative person is trying to move on. But I think if you listen real hard you can still find some of the things, some of that quality that you like in the other person, that’s still there. You might have to search a little harder, and you might have to work a little harder. But it’s probably still there. Again it’s an evolution. So I can’t think of any artists that I liked and all of a sudden just didn’t like. Now there could be artists that maybe over time they have grown on me, which is the other way. Maybe someone at one point I didn’t necessarily understand and now I appreciate. Probably somebody like Led Zeppelin for example. I appreciate them now more. Because I don’t listen to it from a perspective of [finger snaps]. I’m not looking for them to swing. I’m trying to appreciate it from their perspective. See when I was younger I was a jazz snob, where everything to me had to funnel itself at some point from one-two-one-two-three-four. So now I’m understanding that okay, Santana loves what we do but it doesn’t necessarily follow from the hi-hat on two and four and the bass drum on four beats. You know what I mean? You have to be

able to appreciate that for what it is. I can’t go into an Italian restaurant and say man this doesn’t taste like soul food. It’s not supposed to. And so I think as I’ve gotten older I’ve been able to — and I’m still a young man but I’m getting to a point where everybody has all these things to offer. There was a period where I said you know what? I want to play some of the music that influenced me. So you hear me doing [sings] Wake up everybody/no more sleep. So I’m doing that kind of music, where before, when I just left Art and I joined Blue Note Records I probably wouldn’t have recorded any of that, or maybe now I’m doing a Marvin Gaye tune or a Stevie Wonder song. As far as I’m concerned, that’s open game for me. Now I’ve got good friends who would say no way. And guess what? That’s why these different people are able to come and exist and that’s why we have all this wonderful music, because no one thinks the same. Everyone’s got a different way of approaching it, and everybody’s got a different wrinkle to put in it. And I’ve got good friends who do have no inclination or would never record a Stevie Wonder song. And I respect them for that. But for me, I feel that I can grow by doing some different things. It helps me become better. Now they might say well if you stay down this way you will become better. But for me, my nature is to search and to look for some different things, as they probably say they are too. So again, it’s respecting everyone and what they try to do. Because we’re all, at the end of the day, we’re all trying to be better.
It takes every kind of people, right?

It takes every kind of person and I really believe everyone is doing the best they can. And once they try to do better they will. But a person that’s the worst person in the world, believe it or not, that’s just the best he can do. So hopefully he’ll be inspired to do better. So I think at that level it’s very basic.
